question: Create a box plot showing the distribution of TP53 expression levels across different tissue types. Include jittered data points (swarm or strip), proper axis labels, and a title.

files.eval_guideline: Box plot must show TP53 expression across tissue types with individual data points overlaid as jittered points; axis labels, color scheme, and jitter details may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical filename tp53_boxplot.png and PNG image format. The name directly corresponds to the requested box plot of TP53 expression across tissue types.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires visual content: a box plot of TP53 expression across tissue types with overlaid jittered individual points, appropriate axis labels, and a title. Semantic comparison accommodates permitted differences in colors, labels, and jitter placement while checking these required elements.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show box plots of TP53 expression in Brain, Breast, Colon, Liver, and Lung, with individual observations overlaid as horizontally jittered points. The tissue-specific medians, quartiles, whiskers, and observed ranges visually agree: Colon has the highest median expression (approximately 8.2), followed by Brain and Lung (approximately 7.3), Breast (approximately 6.1), and Liver (approximately 5.3). The candidate reorders the tissues by median expression, uses distinct box colors, and adds sample sizes (n=30) and a Kruskal-Wallis p-value. That statistical annotation is additional information whose calculation cannot be verified from the images alone. Both plots have appropriate titles and axis labels and use comparable vertical scales. The reference displays hollow boxplot outlier markers alongside jittered observations, whereas the candidate shows the extreme observations as filled jittered points; this does not change the represented distribution. Differences in styling, category order, and annotation do not materially alter the scientific message.
